description: Hand-labeled detection benchmark (#197). Ground-truth vulnerabilities are labeled from reading each app, independently of what AttackMap emits, so precision/recall are not circular. Only the scored_categories (precise detector classes) are held to precision/recall; advisory/architectural findings are out of scope.

expected.note: Public webhook accepts events with no signature verification.
Privileged, state-changing refund route with no authentication.
Customer record addressed by client-supplied id with no ownership check.
State-changing cancel route with no authentication.
Privileged role-change route with no authentication.
Order addressed by client-supplied id with no ownership check.
Request body interpolated into an f-string SQL INSERT (no parameterization).
Query string concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE clause.
Request-controlled table name interpolated into a REINDEX DDL statement.
State-changing order-creation route with no authentication.
Internal state-changing route with no authentication.
Query value joined into a filesystem path with no basename/containment check (path traversal, two-line flow).
Caller-chosen URL fetched server-side (SSRF, two-line flow). /status/:service is the clean twin (fixed host).
Tokens signed with a 12-character hard-coded HMAC secret; brute-forceable offline from one token.

jsonwebtoken verify with a public key and no algorithms list. jsonwebtoken < 9 accepts an HS256 token signed with the public key; 9.x blocks that swap with a key-type check, but the code still relies on the library default instead of pinning RS256.
Caller identity read from jwt.decode, which does not check the signature. admin.js decodes too, but only to read the header before a pinned verify.
Key file path built from the unverified header kid. adminKey (same file) is the clean twin: a fixed key map.
Sessions signed with express-session's documented example secret 'keyboard cat'.
User stored in the session without regenerate(): a pre-login session id stays valid after login. routes/staff-login.js is the clean twin.
Callback accepts a redirect URI by prefix: https://app.example.com.evil.net passes. routes/partner-sso.js matches exactly.
Authorization request without state (login CSRF). routes/partner-sso.js sends one.
Payment events are applied with no signature check; anyone can mark an invoice paid.
HMAC compared with !==, which leaks timing. routes/github-app.js uses timingSafeEqual and is the clean twin.
Slack signature verified, but X-Slack-Request-Timestamp is never checked, so requests can be replayed. routes/stripe.js (constructEvent) is clean.
